summary: Authenticate native mailbox custody, prove replay recovery and report the declared current harness

replay.detail: No full graph replay is requested. Native delivery reconnects replay the existing fenced mailbox snapshot under stable message identities. A negotiated consumer nonce acknowledgment plus an authenticated current native report proves mailbox recovery; it never completes a turn or authorizes task, tool, input or approval replay.

schema.detail: Store initialization adds the local_mailbox_leases table with the complete subject/component/runtime/provider/session/sequence/PID/process-birth/token/epoch/revocation tuple. Numeric schema and checkpoint rules versions are unchanged. This local custody table persists across daemon reopen and is not erased by reinstalling a binary.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules version or digest changes. Existing complete-card Source/operator certificates do not cover the new mutable lease source or changed harness/fault oracle; successor source capture and pure helper qualification must use the exact integrating source.

compatibility.detail: Linux native admission now requires kernel peer identity, current declared provider, exact physical runtime ancestry/generation and current durable provider ownership. Codex cold startup has a separate physical bootstrap discriminator, promoted without token/epoch/PID change after the real provider claim. Replay frames require the mailbox_replay_ack capability; older clients receive existing frames but cannot prove fault recovery without consumer acknowledgment. Other-platform admission retains its existing behavior. Cross-version provider pairings remain unqualified until their own checks; unchanged public card schema does not preserve the old semantic certificate. Bootstrap admission retains the selected daemon creation stamp and daemon/terminal/peer process births and revalidates their exact managed-wrapper or bound direct-parent relationship under the Store writer. Indeterminate physical queries authorize no mutation and return a retryable unavailable error only after durable capability fencing; retired or foreign capabilities remain terminal. Unfenced older typed reports remain explicit legacy liveness for the declared transport, never current native readiness. Exact-current-runtime provider-neutral diagnostic/modal blocks remain visible without granting missing-provider positive activity.

downtime.detail: Normal Operations daemon/binary deployment applies. Candidate restart-to-API and restart-to-health durations have not been measured. During a live delivery loss the current card shows waiting/indeterminate and the configured owner receives a keyed fault until actual replay recovery is proved.

manual.detail: A still-current pre-lease capability can be authenticated in place without epoch churn. Opaque same-runtime legacy ownership history does not authorize a fresh takeover, and retired tokens remain terminal. Existing reported outages have no established common historical trigger; unsupported or superseded custody needs its configured owner's normal supported recovery action, rather than token deletion, terminal injection or automatic seat restart.

recovery.detail: Authenticated transport reconnect preserves the canonical token/epoch; missing owner metadata can be restored only for that still-current durable lease and existing binding. A dead channel may admit a separately authenticated same-provider/session successor; a captured newer provider owner may take over. Live duplicates, later owners, binding revocation, wrong provider/runtime, terminal completion and intentional stop remain fenced. Roll forward through normal Operations deployment; swapping to a binary that ignores persisted custody is not qualified recovery and does not undo the local schema addition.
